detailedSummary: Outside boundary values force triangle conv{(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)} in the subgradient. Independent local convolution/change-of-variables plus primitive degree1 CLD calibration proves the actual coefficient2 area>=1 on all analytic tests. Positivity survives ordinary collar gluing, and the lower measure bound survives weak/generated limits. The obstruction is restricted to this exact fan class.
text:
Using earlier own n1 for the exactly disclosed analytic calculus, there is a complete new obstruction for EVERY finite translated radial fan with fixed outside-quadrant boundary values, and for every actual generated presentation using such fans. It substantially broadens the previous lambda>1 single-segment failure. It is expressly an obstruction to this specified local class, not all original C/G and not a refutation of unchanged P16.7.

Let H0(b)=max(0,b1)+max(0,b2). Let H be ANY convex finite real affine maximum on R² containing a constant lower slot and satisfying H=H0 whenever b1>=0 OR b2>=0. On the injective chart U define local potential H(log|z1-1|,log|z2-1|)-(1/2)log|z1z2|-1/4, extend its correction to the baseline q0 by zero outside U, and call its weight qH. Theorem: qH belongs to the ENTIRE original C, and MA(qH)>=delta_g, g=sigma(0). Thus at most rawmass1 remains away from g. No qH solves2delta_xc for c>0. Every actual finite-lower-energy decreasing G presentation made of these weights plus constants has the same MA lower bound, as does every weak MA limit of arbitrary families of these bounded fan weights. This covers real slopes, not only integral ones.

Convex proof and actual positivity: every globally active slope lies in[0,1]². Its supporting inequality along b+t ei with the other coordinate positive, as t tends to plus and minus infinity, gives0<=pi<=1. Remove globally redundant planes. Nonnegative slopes and the constant lower slot let every vanishing polynomial slot be omitted on an ordinary neighborhood, after which the remaining slots are real unit logarithms. Positive smooth convex maxima converge locally uniformly; actual harmonic subtraction and minimal-sheaf closure give positivity and continuity at all points. If one original coordinate norm differs from1 then the corresponding translated norm is at least1, so the correction is zero. It therefore vanishes on the genuine ordinary collar1/8<max|ri|<1/4, giving quotient gluing without blind deck descent of zi-1. Convexity between points on the two negative axes gives H<=0 on the negative quadrant, hence qH<=q0 and sup qH=0.

The outside open regions have affine potentials b1, b2 and b1+b2. Their slopes(1,0),(0,1),(1,1) are global supporting slopes of H. Since H(0)=0, they belong to its subgradient polygon P0=partial H(0). Thus P0 contains their triangle, whose Euclidean area is1/2. To turn this into an actual current obstruction, the normalization and support cannot be assumed from tropical geometry; the following complete local comparison establishes them.

For ANY finite convex affine maximum on the translated identity torus near the joint Gauss point of radii b*, the actual Hessian square has atom coefficient2 Area(partial H(b*)). Subtract its value and translate b* to0. On a small real ball inactive planes have a negative gap, so H equals the support function G(b)=max_(p in P) p dot b, P=partial H(0). Convolution with a compact positive smooth kernel gives G_epsilon uniformly tending to G with gradients in P. For any compact P' inside the polygon interior there is a>0 with G(b)-p dot b>=a|b| for every p in P'. On a fixed radius-r ball, the minimum of G_epsilon(b)+delta|b|²/2-p dot b lies inside for sufficiently small epsilon,delta. Its positive-definite Hessian makes its gradient injective with a smooth local inverse. Change of variables identifies the integral of its determinant with its gradient-image area. That image contains P' and lies in P+delta r closed_unit_ball. Let delta go to zero at fixed epsilon, using continuity of the determinant polynomial, then epsilon go to zero and exhaust the polygon interior. Polygon boundary area is zero and outer parallel areas converge to its area; the determinant integral tends to Area(P). If P is a segment or point the same outer-image bound tends to zero. Away from0 every locally active slope belongs to one exposed proper face of P, hence a line, so its local square vanishes by one-dimensional positive convolution. Thus the real determinant measures converge locally to Area(P)delta0.

On the ACTUAL torus in wi=zi-1, any off-joint-Gauss point has a Laurent polynomial with strict cancellation below its monomial maximum. This persists on an ordinary neighborhood whose coordinate tropical values lie in a finite hypersurface of dimension at most1. A coordinate top Hessian form vanishes there. For the identity moment the tangent lattice is saturated and analytic degree1; exact CLD14.5.2--3 and5.10.1(c),(d)/5.10.2 therefore identify the smooth square on the joint Gauss section with2det(Hess G_epsilon)db1db2. A continuous analytic test restricts continuously to that actual Gauss section. The just-proved weak limit gives atom coefficient2 Area(P) on EVERY continuous analytic test, while local uniform recursive-product continuity independently identifies it with the actual Hessian square. Positive Radon reconstruction applies. There is no unspecified analytic multiplicity or radial inverse-measure convention.

At b=0 the translated joint unit Gauss point is exactly the original g, since translation by1 preserves the unit bidisc Gauss norm. The included triangle therefore gives MA(qH)({g})=2 Area(P0)>=1, with the required raw2! normalization. Global positivity and rawmass2 give the mass budget. For every weak limit lambda, all nonnegative continuous tests satisfy int h lambda>=h(g). Regularity/Riesz order yields lambda>=delta_g. The actual canonical operator of an ALREADY actual decreasing G presentation is its weak MA limit, hence satisfies this lower bound. Since xc differs from g, it cannot be2delta_xc. Nothing asserts that general C/G weights have these outside-quadrant values, radial dependence, or such a presentation.

Using earlier own n2, this explains the limitation of its new nested-branch solutions: their off-Gauss mass budget is at most1. It does not show that the whole-mass2delta_x target is ineligible. Indeed n2 with zeta=delta_c gives an actual bounded qc with MA(qc)=delta_g+delta_xc and finite B=D(MA(qc)). For normalized a and C=-E(a), n1 scaling applied to the full dual B yields int(-a)MA(qc)<=1+B+sqrt(6BC). Since2delta_xc<=2MA(qc), its objective is at most-C+2(1+B)+2sqrt(6BC), whose supremum in C>=0 is finite. Thus the original whole target remains eligible and unresolved outside this restricted fan class. The new obstruction is fully calibrated on the actual analytic space; it is not being counted as a complete original obstruction.
